name: objconv
why: Converts object file formats across toolchains; a quiet, useful door into how binaries are structured.

brief.what_it_is: objconv is a command-line object file converter for x86 and x86-64 code. It takes object files, executables, and function libraries in COFF/PE, OMF, ELF, or Mach-O format and converts them between those formats. It can also rename symbols in object files, build and modify function libraries across platforms, and dump object and executable files. The bundled disassembler covers SSE4, AVX, AVX2, AVX512, FMA3, FMA4, XOP, and Knights Corner instructions.
brief.why_it_exists: The page gives no explicit motive. objconv is listed among Agner Fog's software optimization resources, alongside his manuals, vector class library, and assembly function library, so it appears to serve programmers and tool makers who work with binaries across platforms.
brief.install_notes: The page offers objconv only as a download named objconv.zip (about 1 MB) with source code included under the GPL and a manual linked from the same section. The page does not give build steps, dependencies, or a Homebrew formula. The scout's Homebrew entry names the executable as objconv. I did not follow the manual link because its URL was not shown in the page text.
brief.standout: It packs format conversion, symbol renaming, library building, and a fairly capable x86 disassembler into one small GPL tool. Most object-format converters do not also cover this much instruction-set detail in the disassembler.
brief.status: maintained. The objconv.zip download is listed as last modified 2026-May-14, and the page itself shows 2026 update dates for several items. No release version or commit history was visible on the page.
brief.caveats: Only 32-bit and 64-bit x86 platforms are covered, so ARM and other architectures are out of scope. The page describes the tool in a single short paragraph and does not show usage examples. The manual was not read. The homepage is a multi-topic page, not a dedicated project page.
quotes: Can modify symbol names in object files.
Also includes a very good disassembler supporting the SSE4, AVX, AVX2, AVX512, FMA3, FMA4, XOP and Knights Corner instruction sets.

entry.title: objconv
entry.tldr: A small converter that turns x86 object files and libraries between ELF, PE/COFF, OMF and Mach-O, and also disassembles them.
entry.deeper_look:
objconv reads object files, executables and function libraries for 32-bit and 64-bit x86 and writes them back out in another format. The supported formats are COFF/PE, OMF, ELF and Mach-O, so a library built for one platform's toolchain can be reshaped for another's. It can also rename symbols inside an object file, build and modify function libraries, and dump the contents of object and executable files.

It comes from Agner Fog's software optimization resources, which also include his manuals, a vector class library and an assembly function library. The page gives no explicit motive, but the placement suggests it serves programmers and tool makers who ship or consume low-level code across operating systems.

The idea underneath is that an object file is just a container. Machine code, symbol tables and relocations are the same ideas on every platform, and each OS wraps them differently. Converting between wrappers shows what each format actually carries. The bundled disassembler covers SSE4, AVX, AVX2, AVX512, FMA3, FMA4, XOP and Knights Corner instructions, so you can read the code inside the container too.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the tool's usage summary and the options it supports for converting, renaming symbols and dumping files.

entry.whats_unique: It combines format conversion, symbol renaming, library building and a disassembler with wide x86 instruction-set coverage in one small GPL tool.
entry.caveats: It covers only 32-bit and 64-bit x86, so ARM and other architectures are out of scope, and the homepage describes it in one short paragraph with no usage examples.
